Header: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. ciceri Kalae Pae Pin Nyoe in Burmese language

Prevention: Apply green manure for reducing the activity this soil born fusarium wilt disease
Avoid overhead irrigation to prevent disease spreading
Soil solarization by covering it with a transparent polythene sheet for 6-8 weeks during summer
Rotate the crop except with peas and beans varieties with more than 4 year breaks in case of infection
Monitoring: Monitor symptoms in flowing stage (6-8 weeks after sowing) during daytime.
Look for both stem and leave at seedling and flowering stage.
Check leave colour because they change from green to pale green initially, and finally infected leaves will wilt.
There is dark brown discolouration in the internal stem when split open.
Consider preventive action when the wilt disease is known from the area.
Consider action when 5-15% of young plants are infected because the plant can be killed before it reaches maturity.
Action is too late if the disease occured in the late vegetative, flowering and maturity stages of the crop.
Direct Control: Prevention is important as no green direct control is available.
Use seed treatment with non-pathogenic strains such as
Trichoderma biopesticide because it can protect from this soil born fusarium wilt disease
Removal and destruction of disease plants might help in limiting carry-over of the disease in the soil.
Biosynthesis in membrane, (FRAC, G-group); Systemic fungicide applied as seed coating
Restrictions: II products may not be allowed in local
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides
Fungicides can only be used preventively as seed coating.
Fungicides are only effective when applied to seed - spraying is not effective.
Once infected, fields cannot be cured.
Seed coating should be done by trained service providers as seed coating processes can be dangerous to the farmer.
Preferably the farmers should buy coated seeds.
Mitosis and cell division activity on fungal disease (FARC, B1group)
Systemic fungicide applied as seed coating

U (Unlikely acute hazardous to humans); Harmful to soil and water organisms; Moderately harmful to parasitoids and pollinators thus do not spray on flowering crop or near beehives; Slightly harmful to birds and ladybeetle; Possibility of resistance to this fungal disease
